note: The Restoration unfolds across the young United States — from a grove in western New York to a valley in the Rocky Mountains.

places.name: Sharon, Vermont
places.desc: Birthplace of Joseph Smith Jr., December 23, 1805 — a rocky hill farm and a family that read the Bible together.

places.name: Palmyra & Manchester, New York
places.desc: The Sacred Grove, where the Father and the Son appeared in 1820; and the hill Cumorah, where Moroni's plates lay buried. The Book of Mormon was printed on Main Street in 1830.

places.name: Fayette, New York
places.desc: The Whitmer farm — the translation finished, the Three Witnesses shown the plates, and the Church of Christ organized in a log home, April 6, 1830.

places.name: Colesville, New York
places.desc: Home of the Knight family and the church's first branch — and the first miracle of the restored church.

places.name: Harmony, Pennsylvania
places.desc: Emma's hometown, where most of the Book of Mormon was translated — and where John the Baptist restored the Aaronic Priesthood on the Susquehanna's banks, May 15, 1829.

places.name: Kirtland, Ohio
places.desc: The first gathering place, 1831–1838: the School of the Prophets, the vision of the degrees of glory, and a temple where the Savior, Moses, Elias, and Elijah appeared in one afternoon.

places.name: Hiram, Ohio
places.desc: The Johnson farm — Doctrine & Covenants 76 was seen here, and a mob's tar could not stop the work.

places.name: Independence, Missouri
places.desc: Designated the center place of Zion in 1831 — a temple lot dedicated, a printing press raised and wrecked, and a people driven but not released from the dream.

places.name: Liberty Jail, Missouri
places.desc: The 'temple-prison,' winter 1838–39. From its darkness came the light of Sections 121–123: 'Peace be unto thy soul; thine adversity... shall be but a small moment.'

places.name: Far West, Missouri
places.desc: Caldwell County's Latter-day Saint capital — cornerstones laid, revelations received, and the exodus of 1839 begun.

places.name: Adam-ondi-Ahman, Missouri
places.desc: The valley 'where Adam shall come to visit his people' (D&C 116) — a settlement of weeks and a prophecy of ages.

places.name: Nauvoo, Illinois
places.desc: 'The city beautiful,' raised from a malarial swamp on the Mississippi, 1839–1846 — a temple on the bluff, baptism for the dead, and the endowment.

places.name: Carthage, Illinois
places.desc: The jail where Joseph and Hyrum Smith were martyred, June 27, 1844 — 'like a lamb to the slaughter' (D&C 135).

places.name: Winter Quarters, Nebraska
places.desc: The Missouri-River camp of the exiled saints, 1846–47 — where Brigham Young received the order of the Camp of Israel (D&C 136).

places.name: Salt Lake Valley, Utah
places.desc: 'This is the right place.' The gathering's mountain home — and where, in 1918, Joseph F. Smith saw the redemption of the dead (D&C 138).
